papers.title: On Modelling the Scattering of Highly Nonlinear Transient Water Waves Due to Surface-Piercing Cylinder. Part I: Formulations and Verifications
papers.abstract: The presence of extreme ocean waves poses substantial threats to the safety of marine engineering applications and navigational activities. Accurate prediction of the nonlinear wave loads on offshore structures in large-diameter cylindrical configuration, such as monopile wind turbines and platform columns, requires a robust solution to the high-order wave diffraction problem. This paper introduces a novel, highly nonlinear time-domain numerical pseudo-spectrum model based on potential flow theory. By leveraging the Fredholm integral equation of the second kind and Legendre polynomials, a distinct efficient solver for computing the velocity potential on the cylinder surface and vertical velocity at free surface is developed. The present method is verified by comparing with a direct approach based on Fourier transform and established theoretical models for simulating the scattering of small steepness uniform waves. The convergence and computational efficiency of the present method is also demonstrated. The validation of the new model for simulating highly nonlinear transient water waves will be reported in Part II. The proposed model provides a powerful and efficient new framework for analyzing high-order nonlinear wave diffraction and hydrodynamic loads, with significant implications for both scientific research and the engineering design of coastal and offshore structures.

papers.title: Generation of extreme waves with flexible features in fully nonlinear wave models
papers.abstract: Abstract Content of image described in text. We consider the generation of extreme waves of flexible features in deep-water surface gravity waves, in the context of the fully nonlinear wave model, i.e. Euler equations of the free surface. This is achieved through a recently developed GenWave approach, coupled with the high-order spectral method to solve the Euler equations. Through an iterative refinement procedure, GenWave progressively refines the initial phases associated with a given wave spectrum, which leads to extreme-wave generation at specified design time and location, with their probability of exceedance quantified. In this study, we consider two types of extreme waves, enabled by the flexibility of GenWave. The first type is a spatially and temporally localised rogue wave, and second is a spatially localised extreme-wave group propagating at a constant speed. The two generated extreme-wave profiles are compared with their prototypes – the Peregrine soliton and regular soliton (or bright soliton) in the context of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS), with reasonable agreement. For the persistent group, comparison with linear evolution and the NLS identifies nonlinear persistence, faster propagation and bound-wave content beyond the leading-order NLS description.

papers.title: Stochastic interpretation of the Water Waves equations
papers.abstract: The aim of this article is to derive a stochastic interpretation of the Water Waves equations, based on the location uncertainty principle (LU). Next, these equations are used to infer simpler models from scaling limits, such as the Saint-Venant, Boussinesq and Serre-Green-Naghdi ones. Once adapted to the stochastic setting, these models have been successfully implemented numerically, and we show several experiments to assess their properties -- for example the breaking of the wave symmetry, and the influence of time correlated noises.

papers.title: Directional and geometric characteristics of breaking-wave whitecaps in a laboratory wave basin
papers.abstract: The directional characteristics of wave breaking are essential for understanding surface wave dynamics. However, the directional representation of breaking in spectral wave models remains poorly constrained by experimental observations. This study analyzes breaking waves using image processing of whitecaps to extract crest-normal directions and geometric properties. The lower boundary of each active whitecap was used as a proxy for the local breaking-wave crest, with the associated direction defined as normal to the estimated crest. Whitecaps were identified and tracked across multiple cases, and the distribution of their crest-normal directions was compared with the directional spectrum of the wave field. The results indicate that narrower spectral distributions are associated with more focused distributions of crest-normal directions, demonstrating a correspondence between wave directional spreading and the directional organization of breaking crests. Geometric analysis further indicates a power-law relationship between whitecap area and crest length, which warrants further investigation across a broader range of conditions. These findings provide insight into the relationship between breaking-crest geometry and the directional properties of the wave spectrum.

papers.abstract: Climate change and the increasing frequency of extreme weather events pose significant threats to coastal infrastructure, necessitating accurate numerical tools for simulating coastal wave dynamics. papers.title: Reconstruction and Forecast of Extreme Waves from a Single Observation
papers.abstract: The state space of a dynamical system can, under suitable conditions, be reconstructed from a single observational time-series through delay-coordinate embedding. However, reconstructing the spatiotemporal evolution of nonlinear water waves from highly sparse measurements remains a considerable challenge. Here, by combining deep learning, compressed sensing, and the self-similarity properties of unidirectional nonlinear water wave evolution equation, we show that the evolving surface elevation of a highly nonlinear wave field can be reconstructed from observations collected at a {\it single} measurement location. We subsequently use these reconstructions to forecast rogue waves associated with self-focusing soliton dynamics from point observations obtained in controlled water wave tank experiments, demonstrating excellent agreement with measurements of the fully evolved wave field. Our results show that extreme wave events can be forecast from remarkably sparse observations and provide a framework that may be extended to other nonlinear dispersive systems governed by the interplay of dispersion and nonlinearity.

papers.title: Simulation of Breaking Waves in OpenFOAM: Numerical Assessment Using Stokes Wave Initial Conditions
papers.abstract: Understanding the characteristics of breaking waves in deep and intermediate water is essential for both air–sea interaction and wave-structure interaction. This paper explores optimal numerical methods for modelling breaking events within the OpenFOAM framework, using a 2D numerical wave tank. The present work discusses the implementation of initial wave conditions in the OpenFOAM framework and the optimal combination of numerical techniques used for modelling breaking events. Stokes wave theory is used to prescribe the initial wave field, which is first assessed against the corresponding analytical solution before the subsequent nonlinear evolution and breaking processes are investigated. Three orders of Stokes wave theory are used to investigate their capability in simulating wave propagation and modeling a single breaking wave event. Various numerical schemes implemented in OpenFOAM are tested to determine the optimal combination for achieving accurate results. The findings demonstrate that fifth-order Stokes wave theory is the most suitable for capturing the highly nonlinear evolution of waves leading up to breaking.

papers.title: On the spectra of strong turbulence on water surfaces
papers.abstract: Here, I give a brief history of the theory, with twists and turns, and list possible predictions for the spectra of the direct cascade of gravity waves on the water. The description of long waves is straightforward within the weak-turbulence theory developed by Zakharov and his school. As the energy cascade proceeds to shorter scales, the mean surface steepness grows, and wave-breaking events appear with increasing frequency. Considering surface cusps, Phillips suggested a wavenumber spectrum (with a wrong magnitude, as I argue here) and a frequency spectrum whose whole form is incorrect. The right form for the frequency spectral slope due to breaking waves was suggested by Kuznetsov. Here we estimate the magnitude and argue that the frequency spectrum is expected to continue unchanged through the whole cascade. The transition from weak to strong turbulence in the wavenumber and spatio-temporal spectra is due to spectrally nonlocal interactions and happens earlier (at larger scales) than the dimensional estimate suggests. As a result, the magnitude of the strong-turbulence spectrum is not universal but depends on the pumping for a sufficiently long weak-turbulence cascade. The reason for nonlocality is likely that breaking of shorter waves is determined by the magnitude of the longest wave on whose crest they are running.

papers.title: A quantitative measure of predictability for surface gravity waves
papers.abstract: We introduce a Bayesian inference framework to characterize the predictability of a one dimensional ocean surface wave field given surface elevation measurements from a sensor. Unlike the classical theories that only sketch the boundary of a predictable zone based on group velocity, we use the Bayesian posterior uncertainty of surface elevation to quantify the local predictability at every spatiotemporal location. Our approach first constructs a prior distribution to encode existing knowledge of the wave field such as the spectrum and propagation direction. By conditioning on the (possibly noisy) measurement data, we infer the posterior distribution of the wave field, from which a spatiotemporal uncertainty map is extracted. This map agrees well with the group-velocity-based classical predictable zone theory when the frequency spectrum has bounded support. Meanwhile, it also demonstrates predictability even for a spectrum with unbounded frequency support where the classical predictable zone degenerates. A refined analysis of posterior uncertainty using observability Gramian matrix reveals a `data-informed'part and an `un-informed'part of the wave field, with the latter being fundamentally un-predictable. papers.title: Free-surface breaking dynamics and morphology of waves generated by the semi-submerged wedge-shaped body
papers.abstract: The breaking waves at the bow and stern represent a fundamental free-surface phenomenon involving violent interface deformation, air entrainment, and strong two-phase coupling. The temporal evolution and spatial distribution of wave breaking are fundamental to understanding water-air mixing flows around ships. The present study adopts the square stern of high-speed ships as a reference and selects a wedge model as the research object in order to investigate the characteristics of interface breaking and the flow morphology. The free-surface waves around the wedge model were measured using a binocular vision system. A systematic analysis was conducted to investigate the impact of various parameters on the flow patterns in the bow and stern regions. The parameters investigated included draft depth (D), stern width (B), attack angle (α), and draft Froude number FrD=U/gD. The results show that the wave profiles have strong similarity when FrD is chosen as the dominant parameter. The associated parameters of FrD and geometric parameters are found to have a significant influence on the morphological characteristics of the waves.

papers.title: Extended nonlinear theory for water wave modulations under strong winds
papers.abstract: The fourth-order weakly nonlinear theory for modulated wind waves has been derived for a nonlinear-generalized Miles' surface pressure term. The situation of unidirectional waves and a strong wind is considered. The focus is made on the conditions of great and intermediate water depths. Dynamic effects associated with the nonlinear character of the wind–wave interaction have been identified, such as the saturation or intensification of the wind–wave energy exchange, the alteration of the wave and wavegroup shapes including modification of the nonlinear induced flow when the depth is finite, and the complicated picture of the modulational instability. We suggest that a sudden change in wind intensity or direction may contribute to the occurrence of rogue waves due to the wind-dependent bound waves.

papers.abstract: The Arabian Sea Great Whirl (GW) is a large, quasi‐stationary anticyclonic eddy that develops under the southwest monsoon, combining strong surface‐current shear with an energetic and seasonally organized wavefield. This setting provides a distinctive natural laboratory for examining wave–current interactions beyond the transient mid‐latitude regimes emphasized in previous work. Here we ask whether the GW produces a coherent and observable significant‐wave‐height (SWH) footprint, how the relative orientation of waves and currents controls its asymmetry, and how monsoon wind forcing regulates the relative importance of wind‐driven wave growth and current‐induced modulation. We combine multi‐satellite observations with SWAN (Simulating Waves Nearshore) numerical simulations to address these questions. The GW exhibits an asymmetric SWH pattern, with lower SWH where waves and currents align and higher SWH where they oppose, consistent with current‐induced refraction and wave‐energy redistribution. Wave–current modulation strengthens when eddy‐current gradients dominate the background wavefield, while stronger wind‐wave growth diminishes the current signature. Multiscale spectral analysis reveals scale‐dependent redistribution of SWH variability over the resolvable mesoscale range. papers.title: New third-order probability density function for the surface elevation in irregular seas
papers.abstract: Abstract Content of image described in text. We develop saddle-point approximations of the probability density function (PDF) for the surface elevation in nonlinear, irregular seas, without any assumptions regarding uni-directionality of the wave field or narrow-bandedness of the spectrum. A new, closed-form approximation of the PDF at third order is derived, accounting for both skewness and kurtosis. The approximate PDF matches known asymptotics of the third-order positive tail exactly and is free of unphysical oscillations in the negative tail, which widely plague existing PDFs describing nonlinear seas. A normalisation procedure is introduced to enforce unit integral, zero mean and unit variance. We further show that the input cumulants can be adjusted to likewise yield prescribed skewness and kurtosis. Comparison of the new third-order PDF against challenging datasets stemming from irregular wave theory, a fully nonlinear wave model as well as laboratory experiments establishes accuracy. In the Appendix we additionally develop a novel perturbation method, which is used to derive the full form of the asymptotic positive and negative tails at fourth and fifth order, including (previously unknown) prefactors. Collectively, it is shown that even-order solutions inevitably involve oscillatory negative tails, whereas odd orders admit non-oscillatory negative-tail solutions.

papers.title: Lagrangian transport resulting from superposition of surface gravity waves and an internal solitary wave
papers.abstract: Particle transport at the ocean surface is governed by oceanic flows of different scales. In this study, we numerically investigate the collective impact of surface gravity waves (SGWs) and an internal solitary wave (ISW) on free-surface particle transport. By carrying out wave-phase-resolved simulations, we show that adding SGW-induced Stokes drift to the ISW-induced particle displacement acting in isolation does not accurately estimate the displacement resulting from the combined effect of SGWs and the ISW. The ISW-only prediction underestimates the actual ISW-associated displacement by 30–46% in co-propagating configurations and overestimates its magnitude by 200–350% in counter-propagating configurations. The contact time, i.e., the duration for which the particle transport is affected by the ISW-induced current, is found to be longer when SGWs and the ISW co-propagate and shorter for counter-propagation cases with the same ISW magnitude. This asymmetry reveals two distinct mechanisms: the Lagrangian velocities are not additive, and the ISW-modulated SGW orbital velocities and resulting Stokes drift alter the effective drift along the particle trajectories.

papers.title: Modulational stability of finite-depth Stokes waves with constant vorticity
papers.abstract: We investigate the effect of constant vorticity on the modulational spectral stability of small-amplitude periodic gravity waves for the two-dimensional finite-depth water-wave system. We derive an explicit stability criterion that agrees with the prediction obtained by Thomas, Kharif and Manna [43] through a nonlinear Schr\"odinger approximation. For waves propagating to the right, we identify a sharp range of dimensionless positive (counterclockwise) vorticity, for which modulational instability is suppressed at every depth, while at any fixed depth sufficiently strong negative (clockwise) vorticity also restores modulational stability. We give a complete description of the spectrum near the origin and identify a figure-eight spectral curve in the unstable regime. A key distinction from the irrotational case is that the usual Hamiltonian factorization of the linearized operator fails at zero Floquet exponent on the full periodic Sobolev space. We therefore carry out a spectral reduction based on reversibility, without relying on Hamiltonian factorization.

papers.abstract: As offshore wind power development continues to expand into deeper waters, floating offshore wind turbines have attracted widespread attention due to their excellent adaptability to varying water depths and their significant potential for harnessing wind energy resources. Yaw control, as a key technical means for improving the overall energy utilization efficiency of wind farms, can enhance the power generation performance of the entire wind farm by actively altering the direction of the wake to improve the inflow conditions for downstream turbines. papers.abstract: We consider the full two-dimensional water-wave equations in finite depth, with and without surface tension. Water waves have been studied mathematically for more than two centuries. Reflection symmetry remains a common assumption in constructions of periodic steady waves, although asymmetric profiles have been observed in experiments and numerical computations. We construct families of periodic stationary solutions whose free surfaces have no axis of reflection, in both the pure-gravity and capillary--gravity cases. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first rigorous construction of asymmetric periodic pure-gravity waves for the full two-dimensional water-wave problem in finite depth. The proof combines localized vorticity laws with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction. In the pure-gravity case, we introduce a small background shear flow to obtain an invertible boundary operator and couple the interior and free-surface approximations at leading order.

At λ L = 35 and ϵ = 10%, the mean model to prototype ratio of the shoreward peak force coefficient reached 1.23. The differences between model and prototype responses were mainly associated with changes in wave transmission, reverse flow, and vortical motion over and behind the structure as scale decreased. These findings improve the interpretation of reduced model results and support more reliable prototype extrapolation of wave loads on perforated submerged structures.

The full framework includes two steps: the first step to generate an initial (rough) estimation of the wave field using the response-amplitude-operators (RAOs), and the second step to refine the reconstruction using an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) to incorporate the measured motion time series. For all test cases we demonstrate favorable reconstruction of the wave field, which in general further improves with the number of ships available and with uncertain parameters properly estimated. We also provide insights on the successful reconstruction in terms of ensemble correlations between the motion time series and features of the wave field.

papers.abstract: Earth's rotation imposes a dynamical barrier on the free propagation of internal tides at high latitudes, raising questions about the fate of tidal energy poleward of the critical latitude. Satellite observations reveal spiral internal solitary waves (ISWs) along the continental slope of the South Orkney Plateau. Although these waves might be attributed to direct steepening of low‐frequency internal tides, theoretical estimates of their propagation speed are nearly twice those inferred from observations. Using high‐resolution simulations, we resolve this inconsistency by identifying a topographically steered energy cascade: subinertial diurnal internal tides, initially trapped by the slope, undergo nonlinear evolution that generates superinertial harmonics. This frequency upshift allows tidal energy to surpass rotational constraints, radiate offshore, and ultimately evolve into the spiral ISWs. These results identify a distinct energy cascade pathway for internal wave dynamics in polar oceans and demonstrate how tidal energy can be redistributed despite rotational limitations.

papers.abstract: The development of Oscillating Water Column (OWC) devices is hindered by a critical gap in understanding: the neglect of coupling effects between key parameters in the estimation of energy conversion efficiency. papers.abstract: We consider narrow-band deep-water surface gravity waves propagating above a background flow whose spatial scale is comparable to the wavelength. We focus on the regime where the background-flow speed is comparable to the Stokes drift of the waves to derive a two-way coupled model between the fast waves and the slow background flow. Nonlinear wave interactions arise at the same asymptotic order as the two-way coupling and must therefore be included in the derivation. The resulting model consists of a nonlinear version of the reduced wave equation obtained in part I, coupled to a Craik-Leibovich equation governing the evolution of the background flow. The model describes the evolution of the wave field and background flow over the slow turnover frequency of the background flow, thus saving the computational burden of temporally resolving the fast wave frequency. The inviscid model exactly conserves wave action, mechanical energy and horizontal momentum, while the viscous model exactly conserves horizontal momentum. The coupling terms are cast in compact form for ease of physical interpretation and numerical implementation.

papers.title: Radiation and persistent shape dynamics for the five-dimensional energy-critical nonlinear wave equation
papers.abstract: We consider the nonradial five-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. We construct a forward-global solution which remains arbitrarily close to a nondegenerate sign-changing stationary state in the energy space and is asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave. The stationary profile moves in a compact conformal family, but its limit set contains a continuum of classes modulo translations, dilations and rotations. Consequently, the solution admits no soliton resolution using a fixed finite collection of stationary profiles and fixed Lorentz velocities, with pairwise orthogonal spatial parameters. That is, we disprove the fixed-profile soliton resolution conjecture for the five-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. The construction uses a sequence of incoming waves with summable energies. Their quadratic impulses produce fixed shape displacements on increasing time scales. The main estimates control the zero eigenvalue of the linearized operator and the nonlinear error uniformly over the entire sequence. The stationary input uses a computer-assisted spectral bound for a symmetric single-node state.

papers.title: Reproduction of critical wave events for the design of floating offshore structures
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Maritime Engineering
papers.abstract: This work presents a methodology for identifying and reproducing critical wave events that induce extreme mooring line tension in floating offshore wind turbines. The approach begins with fully non-linear sea-state realisations, generated using a JONSWAP spectrum and propagated via a fully non-linear potential flow solver. The Hilbert transform is applied on the linear component obtained from a four-wave spectral decomposition process of the surface elevation, to extract amplitude envelopes and instantaneous phase information, enabling the isolation of critical wave events responsible for extreme structural responses. Each critical wave event is expressed as a sum of focused wave groups using a Gaussian envelope regression methodology, allowing for individual iterative amplitude correction and phase focusing to overcome the challenges of reproducing steep wave events. The corrected focused wave groups are then recombined to create a ‘Hyper-Group’ with accurate spatial and temporal focusing at the desired location. The reproduced event is numerically validated against the original sea-state, demonstrating very good agreement in induced mooring line tension. This methodology provides an efficient framework for generating realistic design waves, supporting targeted numerical and experimental testing of floating offshore wind turbines under extreme conditions.

papers.title: Freeze, Then Select: Structured Field Adapters and Stability-Validated Weak Selection for PDE Discovery from Sparse Observations
papers.abstract: PDE discovery from sparse observations requires reconstructing a continuous field and selecting the correct differential terms. Our analysis of optimization paths in coupled neural PDE discovery reveals three behaviors: the exact support can persist to the end of training, appear only transiently, or fail to emerge. To decouple equation selection from neural optimization, we develop a freeze-then-select method combining a structured field adapter with Stability-Validated Weak Selection (SVWS). Trained from observations without a PDE residual, the adapter factorizes the field into learned spatial features and temporal coefficients represented by cubic splines. After freezing the field, SVWS identifies recurrent terms across independent weak-form systems, refits candidate supports, and selects the final equation on held-out weak-form systems. Beyond fixed libraries, we apply the same principle to expressions generated by genetic programming and recover the power-law form of an unknown nonlinear diffusion function from sparse, noisy observations. Across all six sparse MDBench regimes, our method attains the highest exact support recovery rate, with its clearest gains over classical and neural baselines on challenging Kuramoto-Sivashinsky dynamics.

papers.title: Hypothesize, Evaluate, Refine: A Scientific Agent for PDE Discovery with Unknown Spatial Coefficient Fields
papers.abstract: Discovering PDEs in heterogeneous media requires jointly identifying the governing operator and the unknown spatial fields that parameterize it. These tasks are coupled: changing field placement changes the differential law, while a sufficiently flexible field can conceal structural error on a single trajectory. We present Hypothesize, Evaluate, Refine for PDE Discovery (HER-PDE), a scientific-agent framework that discovers compositional PDE structure together with nonparametric, time-invariant coefficient fields. The Agent analyzes two noisy trajectories generated by different excitations, proposes complete expression-tree hypotheses, and combines creative structural exploration with local candidate refinement. Its Hypothesis Evaluation Interface (HEI) estimates only the fields explicitly declared in each hypothesis, never adds missing terms, and scores structures by bidirectional cross-excitation transfer. The selected law is subsequently audited on a sealed temporal interval. Across five controlled two-dimensional systems observed with 5 percent relative Gaussian state noise, the Agent recovers the generating operator in all five cases, including equivalent signed-field and product-rule parameterizations. Across nine unknown coefficient fields, the recovered fields attain a median Pearson correlation of approximately 0.85 and a median relative L2 error of approximately 0.28.
